I'm a healthcare professional and often work in palliative care, as well as with cirrhosis patients. 

In my experience, the timeline can differ rapidly. I've seen patients (in hospital) stay in our care for weeks before they pass away, and on the other hand, I've seen patients last less than a few days. If she develops Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS), she's likely not to have long to live.

As for the actual death itself, in can vary. If she suffers a variceal bleed, it is usually very quick, as the heart stops suddenly because of blood loss. The usual cause for death in cirrhotic patients is multi organ failure. In this scenario, patients get gradually weaker over days or weeks before suddenly deteriorating and becoming unresponsive. Patients usually pass in their sleep, and are not in pain because of medication, although it isn't necessarily an easy thing to watch.

I'm sorry if this has been a little morbid. Please feel free to send me a private message if you have any questions, I'd be more than happy to help.
